newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sells HRK195 mln 42-day bills, rate falls.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sells HRK195 mln 42-day bills, rate falls.

text.p: Croatia's Finance Ministry said it raised 195 million kuna in 42-day treasury bills at a primary auction on Tuesday.
The amount overshot its target by 45 million kuna on total bids of 202.7 million, it said in a news release.
The new issue was priced higher at 98.975 percent from 98.946, at a single interest rate of 9.0 percent.
The issued rate fell from 9.26 percent at the end of May, when 42-day bills were last sold. Full results on page MFHT.
Banking sector bought 97.90 percent of the issue. Auctions are not open to foreign investors though they can place their bids through Croatian banks.
The ministry said it had 506 million kuna in outstanding 42-, 91- and 182-day bills.
It set the next auction for July 15, when it will offer investors 40 million kuna 182-day bills. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
